overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of company safety commitments and the criticisms of them. You'll be asked about frontier safety frameworks, how commitments are checked, the criticism that commitments are too weak, and the regulatory-capture and open-model arguments.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A developer's published policy says that if a model can give real help to someone making a biological weapon, the model won't be released until specified protections are in place. What is this an example of?

options.html: A binding rule set by a regulator
options.text: A binding rule set by a regulator
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A binding rule is set by law and carries a penalty. This is a company's own promise linking a capability to safeguards, which is an if-then commitment.

options.html: A safety index graded by outsiders
options.text: A safety index graded by outsiders
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A safety index is a scorecard that grades companies. This is a company's own promise linking a capability to safeguards, which is an if-then commitment.

options.html: An if-then commitment in a framework
options.text: An if-then commitment in a framework
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The policy ties a stated capability threshold to stated safeguards: if the model reaches the threshold, then the protections must be in place.

options.html: A whistleblower protection for employees
options.text: A whistleblower protection for employees
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Whistleblower protections concern employees who report dangers. This is a company's own promise linking a capability to safeguards, which is an if-then commitment.

forms.stemHtml: Who decides whether a model has reached a capability threshold in a company's frontier safety framework?

options.html: The company that wrote the framework
options.text: The company that wrote the framework
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The company writes the framework, decides whether a threshold has been reached, and chooses the safeguards. That is why critics ask who checks.

options.html: A government regulator with veto power
options.text: A government regulator with veto power
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Government safety institutes test models under voluntary agreements and can't block a release. The company itself decides whether a threshold has been reached.

options.html: A panel of the summit's host countries
options.text: A panel of the summit's host countries
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The governments that hosted the Seoul summit announced the commitments and don't enforce them. The company itself decides whether a threshold has been reached.

options.html: An international court of AI experts
options.text: An international court of AI experts
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No such court exists. The company itself decides whether a threshold has been reached.

forms.stemHtml: Government institutes, outside evaluators, and employees can all help check a company's safety commitments. What weakness do the three routes share?

options.html: Each is paid for by the company being checked
options.text: Each is paid for by the company being checked
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Government institutes are publicly funded. The shared weakness is that each route depends on access the company grants and can withdraw.

options.html: Each is limited to models already released
options.text: Each is limited to models already released
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Some institutes and evaluators test models before release. The shared weakness is that each route depends on access the company grants and can withdraw.

options.html: Each is barred by law from publishing results
options.text: Each is barred by law from publishing results
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No general law bars publication. The shared weakness is that each route depends on access the company grants and can withdraw.

options.html: Each depends on access the company grants
options.text: Each depends on access the company grants
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Institutes rely on voluntary agreements, evaluators on the access they're given, and employees on contract terms and channels the company sets.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these are part of the criticism that company safety commitments are too weak or are weakening? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Companies revise commitments when rivals don't follow them
options.text: Companies revise commitments when rivals don't follow them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Critics argue that competitive pressure makes a voluntary commitment weakest when a rival is about to get ahead.

options.html: A 2026 index graded no company above C+ overall
options.text: A 2026 index graded no company above C+ overall
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The Future of Life Institute's index is the critics' most systematic evidence. Its publisher campaigns for stronger regulation.

options.html: Safety rules mainly help large firms block small rivals
options.text: Safety rules mainly help large firms block small rivals
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is the regulatory-capture critique, which points in the opposite direction: it fears binding rules, where the "too weak" critics want them.

options.html: Only rules binding on every company will hold
options.text: Only rules binding on every company will hold
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The remedy these critics propose is a binding rule, so that no company loses ground by meeting the standard.

forms.stemHtml: An international expert report accepts that open-weight models help research and widen access. What risk does it say is particular to them?

options.html: They cost more to run than closed models
options.text: They cost more to run than closed models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Cost isn't the risk the report identifies. It says that released weights can't be recalled and that safeguards are easier to remove.

options.html: Released weights can't be recalled
options.text: Released weights can't be recalled
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Once weights are published, the developer can't take them back, and the report adds that safeguards on such models are easier to remove.

options.html: They are owned by a few large companies
options.text: They are owned by a few large companies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Concentration of ownership is the concern raised about closed models. The report says that released weights can't be recalled and that safeguards are easier to remove.

options.html: They can't be inspected by outsiders
options.text: They can't be inspected by outsiders
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Open-weight models can be inspected by anyone, which is one of the arguments for them. The report says that released weights can't be recalled and that safeguards are easier to remove.

title: Company self-governance and its critics
